name: Dodo Knief
blurb: The wedding of her brother Paul, her own live-wire reputation as a columnist -- and the 35 poems and essays, the single largest contribution by any Mueller, that Dora wrote for the *Sängerbote*, a German-Lutheran literary quarterly.

name: Mark and Alli's Christmas Letters
blurb: Annual Christmas letters get a mixed reception: tossed unread, browsed lightly, responded to. In the aggregate, though, they have some historical value — some bits of information about who's doing what. So here's the archive.

name: The Chicago Memoirs
blurb:
In 1967 Joel Nickel accepted a call to Our Redeemer Lutheran Church in Englewood, on Chicago’s South Side — a 1,700-seat "Cathedral of Gospel Art" built for a congregation that had long since moved to the suburbs. His predecessor’s advice was "Don’t come."

He and Susan stayed five years: through the Parker High School walkout, the riots that followed Martin Luther King’s murder, the Disciples asking to meet in the parish hall, and the slow collapse of the buildings around them. The congregation was really two — a white Sunday congregation driving in from the suburbs and a black weekday one from the neighbourhood — and most of the story is the effort to make them one church.

Written from notes in 1973, and in his own words "not a success story."

name: My Life and Its Times
blurb: Mary Allison (Molly) Bigelow McMillan had a lot to distill into a memoir: daughter of a long-established Twin Cities family, physics graduate of Vassar, war-time bride, civic leader, and among the first ordained Presbyterian women in Minnesota.

name: Adelheid Rickmeyer, Frau Erica
blurb: The Frau Erica of the archive's name: her cookbook, and the poems, hymn texts and one essay she contributed to the *Sängerbote*, a German-Lutheran literary quarterly.

name: *Winke für Auswanderer*
blurb: Carl de Haas arrived on the Wisconsin frontier in 1847. His booklet of advice for people considering emigration was widely available in Germany and went through at least two printings.

name: Ernst and Helen Mueller
blurb: The Muellers of Freedom Township, and life in the bakerhouse, 1911-1948 -- plus the eight poems and one unpublished sequel Ernst (Opa) contributed to the *Sängerbote*, a German-Lutheran literary quarterly.

name: Fritz Mueller's Journal of the Voyage to America
blurb: Fritz Mueller kept a journal of the 1865 crossing and the journey inland. The archive holds both his German and the English translation made by his great-grandson Herbert, set side by side.

name: Ludwig Knief's *Lebenslauf*
blurb: Written from memory in August 1902 and addressed to his children: a farm childhood near Bremen, the California gold rush, and a life in the ministry in America. German and English side by side.

name: Fred Knief
blurb: A brother-in-law's account of a Mueller wedding, and the story of his own -- plus the four essays Fred contributed to the *Sängerbote*, a German-Lutheran literary quarterly.

name: Gerhard Mueller
blurb: The pastor of Height of Land: his life, the parish he was proudest of, a sportswriter's afternoon at the state basketball tournament, the record of his estate, and the road trip the archivist drove through northern Minnesota in 1980 to find the people who still remembered him.

name: Alida Wood Bigelow: Memories
blurb: Written at her daughter Emma's insistence — "It seems to me a foolish undertaking," Alida begins, "as every scrap of paper or records that might help went up in smoke long ago."

name: Wilhelm and Frau Erica
blurb: Wilhelm Mueller and Adelheid, the Frau Erica this archive is named for: Kendallville, then careers in Chicago.

name: Jim Nickel: Three Cities
blurb: Oak Park, Brentwood, New York — a life told through the places it was lived in.

name: Joel Nickel
blurb: Forty years of ministry, and a second life in art.

name: The Waldschmidts
blurb: Anna's history, and Henry's.

name: H.C. Nickel
blurb: Stock seller, teacher, and a newspaper column on money and happiness.

name: Kevin McKibbin
blurb: Park ranger. Remembered in his obituary and in an account of the work.

name: The Bethlehem Congregation Case
blurb: A minister sued his congregation in St. Louis, and the proceedings were published in German.

name: The Rev. E.H.C. Mueller
blurb: Two obituaries of the same man, one in English and one in German.

name: Tante Fieks
blurb: Frieda Mueller — Tante Fieks — looking back on bright and dark days.
